The instant appeal under Section 14A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant against the order dated 6.3.2024 passed by learned Special Judge, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act Cases, Bikaner in a pair of Cr. Misc. Bail Applications led by Cr. Misc. Bail Application No.473/2024, whereby the bail application filed by the appellant (Cr. Misc. Bail Application No.475/2024), who has been arrested in connection with FIR No.162/2023 registered at Police Station Khajuwala, District Bikaner, for offences punishable under Sections 376-D and 376A, 109,
119, and 120-B of IPC and [2024:RJ-JD:22143] (2 of 4) [CRLAS-534/2024] Sections 3(2)(va),
3(2)(v), 3(2)(vi) and 3(2)(vii) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, has been rejected.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Learned counsel submitted that the co-accused persons namely Rakesh Kumar (CRLAS No.163/2024) and Bhagirath Saharan (CRLAS No.2588/2023) have already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide orders dated 15.3.2024 and 26.2.2024.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the FIR and the challan papers, learned counsel submitted that the specific allegation of sexual assault - rape has been levelled by the complainant and other relatives of the deceased against the co-accused Dinesh Kumar.
Learned counsel further submitted that the presence of the appellant at the place of incident has not been shown/established by the prosecution.

Learned counsel submitted that the only allegation against the present appellant is that he took the deceased to the hospital after the alleged incident alongwith co-accused Bhagirath Saharan, who has already been enlarged on bail by this Court.

Attention of the Court was further drawn towards the statements of one Rajendra Singh - Constable recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. to state that at the time of incident, the appellant was sitting with him in the police quarters alongwith co-accused Bhagirath Saharan and on receiving one phone call, the appellant left the quarter with him to reach the place of incident.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the investigation against the appellant has already been completed, the appellant is in judicial custody and the trial of the case will take sufficiently [2024:RJ-JD:22143] (3 of 4) [CRLAS-534/2024] long time, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-appellant.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application.
However, they were not in a position to refute the fact that the co- accused persons namely Rakesh Kumar and Bhagirath Saharan have already been enlarged on bail by this Court.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and after perusing the challan papers, statements of the various witnesses recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and analysis of the CCTV footages recovered during the course of investigation, this Court also prima facie finds that the presence of the appellant at the place of incident has not been established during the course of investigation.

This Court prima facie finds that the case of the present appellant is not distinguishable from that of the case of co-accused Bhagirath Saharan, who has already been enlarged on bail by this Court in CRLAS No.2588/2023.

This Court also prima facie finds that the specific allegation of sexual assault - rape has been levelled by the complainant and other relatives of the deceased against co- accused Dinesh Kumar; the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of appellant influencing the material witnesses of the case or fleeing away from justice, in case he is enlarged on bail.

Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of [2024:RJ-JD:22143]
(4 of 4) [CRLAS-534/2024] the case, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant deserves to be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text:
The order dated 6.3.2024 passed by learned Special Judge,
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases, Bikaner is set aside and it is ordered that the accused-appellant- Manoj Kumar S/o Shri Ghanshyam shall be enlarged on bail in connection with FIR No.162/2023 registered at Police Station Khajuwala, District Bikaner,
provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/-
each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to so.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 32-TarunGoyal/-
